Quantify identified components (Polyarc)

quantify.Rd

Converts raw FID component areas to amounts using the Polyarc response model $$m_i = m_t \frac{F_i}{F_t} \frac{C_t}{C_i} \frac{M_i}{M_t}$$ where F is the FID area, C the carbon count and M the molar mass.

Usage

quantify(result, info, style = NULL, reference_peak = NULL)

Arguments

result

A moosaic_result after identify_components().

info

Sample metadata from sample_info().

style

"internal" (relative to a reference peak), or an external calibration curve: "slope", "slope_intercept" or "quadratic". NULL uses option moosaic.quant_style.

reference_peak

Component id of the reference peak for style = "internal"; NULL picks the largest well-identified peak. Ignored for external styles.

Value

result with a peaks tibble (one row per analyte component by retention time: the peak table columns plus origin, family, solvent, amount_ug_ml, wt_pct, quant_basis and calibration_target) and a quant list (style, reference_peak, info).

Details

Only the raw (unsmoothed) FID component areas are used. Peaks without an identification receive an estimated formula by interpolation along the run (see .interpolate_unknowns()), so every peak is quantified. With "internal", amounts are normalised to total 1e6 * density ug/mL (100 wt%); the reference peak is marked "Target". With an external curve, calibration targets found in the sample (matched by name) are read off their curve, scaled by the dilution, and all other peaks are scaled from the nearest preceding target of the same type (hydrocarbon or oxygenate). Calibration points with a zero response are treated as below detection. Overlapping components share the raw FID area according to the fitted profiles (see .apportion_fid_area()).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- identify_components(deconvolve_run(exp))
quantify(res, sample_info("S1", density = 0.85))$peaks
} # }
